title: A raw rational Cauchy bound at TWO DIFFERENT sample indices lifts to a CReal closeness bound
statement: If the m-th rational sample of x and the n-th rational sample of y are within k of each other (the raw, Rat-level Within predicate, at potentially DIFFERENT indices m and n for the two sides), then x and y are close as CReal values: |x - y| <= ofRat(k + 1/(m+1) + 1/(n+1)). This generalizes the already-registered F:creal-close-within-of-within (which shares one index n for both x and y) to two INDEPENDENT sample indices, absorbing one self-approximation gap for whichever index each side actually used. This is the bridge CReal.riemannSum_sharedAccuracyClose_at's own kind of argument needs, where the two sides of a comparison are not sampled at the same accuracy-driven index.

formal.statement: theorem CReal.close_within_of_within_indexed : ((x0 : CReal) -> ((x1 : CReal) -> ((x2 : AxNat) -> ((x3 : AxNat) -> ((x4 : Rat) -> ((x5 : CReal.Within (Rat.sub (CReal.seq x0 x2) (CReal.seq x1 x3)) x4) -> CReal.le (CReal.abs (CReal.add x0 (CReal.neg x1))) (CReal.ofRat (Rat.add x4 (Rat.add (Rat.natDivSucc (AxNat.succ AxNat.zero) x2) (Rat.natDivSucc (AxNat.succ AxNat.zero) x3))))))))))
